title: Statistics, Correlation & Probability
description: Mixed-format quiz (MCQ, true/false, select-all) on measures of central tendency, variance & standard deviation, data dispersion, covariance & correlation, probability, random variables, conditional probability, and Bayes' theorem — aligned with the university question bank (Q16–Q24).

questions.question: Which measure of central tendency is calculated by summing every value in a dataset and dividing by the count?
options: Mean
Median
Mode
Variance

questions.question: Which measure of central tendency is the middle value when data is sorted in order, and is far less affected by outliers than the mean?
options: Median
Mean
Mode
Standard deviation

questions.question: Which measure of central tendency is the value that occurs most frequently, and is the only one usable meaningfully for categorical (non-numeric) data?
options: Mode
Median
Mean
Covariance

questions.question: Why is the median often preferred over the mean for skewed, outlier-prone data such as income or house prices?
options: The median depends only on position, so it is far less affected by extreme values than the mean
The median cannot be calculated for numerical data
The mean is always identical to the mode
The median requires more computation than the mean
questions.answer: The median depends only on position, so it is far less affected by extreme values than the mean

questions.question: What does variance measure about a dataset?
options: The average of the squared differences between each value and the mean
The single value that occurs most often
The middle value once the data is sorted
The strength of the relationship between two variables
questions.answer: The average of the squared differences between each value and the mean

questions.question: Why is standard deviation often preferred over variance when interpreting spread?
options: It is expressed in the same units as the original data, unlike variance which is in squared units
It is always a negative number, unlike variance
It completely ignores the mean of the data
It cannot be computed for any real dataset
questions.answer: It is expressed in the same units as the original data, unlike variance which is in squared units

questions.question: A low standard deviation in a dataset indicates that:
options: Data points are clustered tightly around the mean
Data points are widely spread out over a large range
The dataset has no defined mean
The dataset must be categorical, not numerical
questions.answer: Data points are clustered tightly around the mean

questions.question: What does a positive covariance between two variables indicate?
options: The variables tend to increase or decrease together
The variables always move in exactly opposite directions
There is no relationship between the two variables at all
One variable is always numerically larger than the other
questions.answer: The variables tend to increase or decrease together

questions.question: What is the main limitation of covariance as a way to compare the strength of relationships between different pairs of variables?
options: Its magnitude depends on the units of the variables, so it cannot be easily compared across different variable pairs
It can never be a negative number
It only applies to categorical variables
It always equals zero whenever variables are related
questions.answer: Its magnitude depends on the units of the variables, so it cannot be easily compared across different variable pairs

questions.question: How does correlation improve on covariance as a measure of relationship?
options: It standardizes covariance into a unit-free value between -1 and +1, making strength comparable across different variable pairs
It removes the need to ever calculate a mean
It can only ever describe negative relationships
It is always numerically identical to the variance
questions.answer: It standardizes covariance into a unit-free value between -1 and +1, making strength comparable across different variable pairs

questions.question: A correlation coefficient of r = -0.9 indicates:
options: A strong negative linear relationship
A strong positive linear relationship
No relationship at all between the variables
An impossible/invalid value, since correlation cannot be negative

questions.question: A correlation coefficient of r = 0 indicates:
options: No linear relationship between the variables, though a non-linear relationship could still exist
A perfect positive linear relationship
A perfect negative linear relationship
That the two variables are exactly identical
questions.answer: No linear relationship between the variables, though a non-linear relationship could still exist

questions.question: "Correlation is not causation": two variables can rise together because a hidden third factor drives both of them, rather than one variable directly causing the other.
options: True
False

questions.question: Probability is always expressed as a number between 0 (the event is impossible) and 1 (the event is certain).
options: True
False

questions.question: A discrete random variable can take any value within a continuous range, such as a person's exact height.
options: True
False

questions.question: Bayes' theorem provides a formal, principled way to update the probability of a hypothesis as new evidence is observed.
options: True
False

questions.question: Which of the following are measures of central tendency?
options: Mean
Median
Mode
Standard deviation

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of datasets that typically show HIGH data dispersion (spread)?
options: Real estate prices in a large city
Incomes in a country
Test scores in a very easy exam
Adult heights in a specific population
answer: Real estate prices in a large city

questions.question: In Bayes' theorem, P(A|B) = [P(B|A) · P(A)] / P(B), which of the following terms are correctly named?
options: P(A) is the prior probability
P(B|A) is the likelihood
P(A|B) is the posterior probability
P(B) is called the likelihood

questions.question: Which of the following are true about conditional probability, P(A | B)?
options: It is the probability of event A occurring, given that event B has already occurred
Knowing that B occurred can change the estimated likelihood of A
It is always exactly equal to the unconditional probability of A
It restricts attention to the part of the sample space where B has occurred
answer: It is the probability of event A occurring, given that event B has already occurred
Knowing that B occurred can change the estimated likelihood of A
It restricts attention to the part of the sample space where B has occurred
